new_public_evidence.source: Douc, Cappe, Moulines, Comparison of Resampling Schemes for Particle Filtering
new_public_evidence.result: Explicit interleaved two-value counterexample: systematic resampling can retain O(1) conditional variance as n grows, while multinomial and stratified/residual decrease as O(1/n).

derived_results.claim: For alternating x1/x0 particles with total q mass omega on x1, multinomial variance is omega(1-omega)/n, stratified/residual is (2omega-1)(1-omega)/n and systematic is (omega-1/2)(1-omega), so systematic/stratified=n/2 for omega>1/2.
At omega=0.75,n=64 the variances are 0.0625 systematic, 0.0029296875 multinomial and 0.001953125 stratified: systematic is 21.33x multinomial and 32x stratified.

Because the failure already occurs in the q=W special case, semantic/proxy ordering can create resampling aliasing even without aggressive importance weights. Ordering must be logged and tested if a shared-offset systematic allocator is used.

Random permutation can empirically break the counterexample but adds shuffle/reproducibility cost and no universal variance theorem. Independent stratified uniforms retain the r120 variance guarantee, so they remain the robust default.

engineering_update.scope: Exact algebraic mapping of the published resampling counterexample; no real-agent benchmark yet.

negative_or_scope_evidence: Adversarial counterexample does not imply systematic is usually bad.
Stratified is also ordering-sensitive in distribution, but keeps its conditional variance dominance over multinomial.
Correctness and variance are separate; proper weighting can make systematic valid even when inefficient.
frontier: Implement a multi-generation recursive synthetic tree under r121 weights and compare stratified/systematic/iid across sorted/alternating/random orderings.
Derive predictable particle-count value-of-information allocation tied to r119 material evidence demand.
Measure genealogical diversity/ESS under defensive floor changes across generations.
Map to real multi-turn agent evaluation only after base/proposal transition likelihood semantics are explicit.

Verify mean normalizing-constant correctness for all properly weighted versions, compare variance and genealogy diversity, and use the result to decide whether systematic deserves any implementation path at all.
